findings.title: S3 bucket without server-side encryption
findings.description: S3 buckets should encrypt objects at rest. A bucket with no server_side_encryption_configuration block relies on the account default, which may not exist. Standalone aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration resources are acknowledged but require graph correlation to attribute.

findings.title: S3 bucket without versioning
findings.description: Versioning protects against accidental deletion and overwrites and is required for reliable recovery. Provider default is disabled.
findings.remediation: Enable data protection. Turn on versioning / point-in-time recovery / automated backups with a retention period ≥ 7 days (30+ for production). Test restores regularly — untested backups are not backups.

findings.title: S3 bucket without public access block
findings.description: Without an aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block enabling all four protections (block_public_acls, block_public_policy, ignore_public_acls, restrict_public_buckets), a single permissive ACL or policy can expose the bucket. Fail-safe: only a proven all-four-true block silences this rule.

evidence.actual: absent or not all four protections enabled
evidence.expected: public access block with all four settings = true

findings.remediation:
Add the public access block resource (see AEGIS-AWS-003 fix). All four settings
must be true for full protection.

findings.title: S3 bucket policy does not enforce TLS (SecureTransport)
findings.description: Without an explicit Deny on aws:SecureTransport=false, bucket objects can be fetched over plaintext HTTP. Add a bucket policy statement denying s3:* when SecureTransport is false.

evidence.expected: bucket policy denying s3:* when SecureTransport is false

findings.remediation: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

findings.title: S3 bucket without server access logging
findings.description: Server access logging records requests against the bucket, which is essential for audit and incident response.
findings.remediation: Enable audit logging. Turn on CloudTrail (multi-region, log file validation, KMS-encrypted bucket), VPC flow logs, and service access logs. Ship logs to a dedicated, MFA-delete-protected bucket in a security account.

findings.title: S3 bucket without lifecycle configuration
findings.description: Hygiene: S3 buckets should define lifecycle rules to transition or expire objects, controlling long-term storage costs. Add a lifecycle_rule block or an aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration resource.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Key Vault without firewall
findings.description: A Key Vault with no network_acls block, or with network_acls.default_action = "Allow", accepts connections from any network. Restrict access with default_action = "Deny".
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Key Vault not using RBAC authorization
findings.description: azurerm_key_vault with enable_rbac_authorization = false uses legacy access policies. Prefer Azure RBAC for centralized access control.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Key Vault network ACLs allow public traffic
findings.description: azurerm_key_vault without a network_acls block (default allow) or with default_action other than "Deny" accepts secret/key operations from any network. Set default_action = "Deny" with explicit allowances.
findings.remediation: Remove public exposure. Restrict ingress to known CIDR ranges, move the resource into private subnets, and front it with a load balancer or API gateway if external access is required. Verify with `aws ec2 describe-security-groups`.
